My Niyyah

Product Designer

2 Team Members

3 Months (2025)

Collaborative Personal Project

My Niyyah is a spiritual habit tracker for Muslims who want to build consistency without turning worship into another productivity metric.

See the Product Showcase

The Challenge

Too Much Noise

We wanted prayer tracking to feel focused rather than another content-heavy experience.

Too Much Streaks

We wanted consistency to feel supportive without turning worship into a productivity metric.

Reflection is Hard to Sustain

We wanted Muhasabah to have enough structure to become part of the routine.

Design Direction

A companion, not a judge.

Instead of treating spirituality like another productivity system, we designed My Niyyah around three steps: Act, Reflect, and Understand.

Act

quickly track daily prayers.

Reflect

use guided prompts for Muhasabah.

Understand

review patterns over time without relying on perfect streaks.

The goal was to make consistency feel supportive rather than punitive.

MVP Features

Quick Prayer Tracking

A quick, low-friction way to log daily prayers without interrupting the worship experience.

Meaningful Insights

Weekly patterns that help users recognize progress without turning spiritual consistency into a perfect-streak metric.

Guided Muhasabah

Gentle prompts for evening journaling to help users move beyond checking boxes and start understanding their heart's condition.

Design Language

Visual Persona

Calm, serene and grounded.

Typography and Colors

Using soft, calming blue-green tones and generous whitespace to create a calm and focused experience.

What I Learned

This project helped me become more intentional about how information is structured, prioritized, and translated into a clear visual experience.

Hierarchy Changes Meaning

I learned that good UI is not only about arranging elements neatly. The order, size, spacing, and emphasis of information strongly affect what users notice first.

Layout Needs Purpose

I became more comfortable using spacing, alignment, and grouping to create clearer sections instead of treating layout as a purely visual exercise.

Less Can Say More

Working on a focused product taught me to be more selective. Not every feature or piece of information needs to compete for attention.

Design for Collaboration

Working with a developer also taught me to think beyond the design file and communicate decisions clearly enough for another person to turn them into a working product.

What I'd Improve

Looking back, the biggest opportunity was in strengthening the evidence and process behind the decisions I made, not only in the final UI.

Do More Competitive Research

I did not document enough comparisons with existing Islamic apps and habit trackers. Next time, I would use competitive research to validate assumptions and identify clearer opportunities.

Validate Before Designing

Some of the problems I identified were based more on assumptions than direct user evidence. I would validate these assumptions through interviews, usability testing, or lightweight user feedback.

Document the Reasoning

I focused heavily on the final interface, which meant some of the reasoning behind my decisions was not captured. Next time, I would document key iterations and trade-offs as I work.

Measure the Outcome

The project reached a working MVP, but I did not establish clear measures of success. Next time, I would define simple goals and test whether the design actually supports them.
